subject: Re: DPA & cross-border handling — training exclusion & prompt ownership
messages:
From: Elena Hernandez <elena.hernandez@greenleaf.health>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenleaf.health
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:12:00 +01:00
Subject: DPA questions — training exclusion, prompt ownership, cross-border transfers

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for sending the latest DPA draft (attached). Before we loop legal, a couple of high-level questions from our security and procurement teams so we can prioritize: 

1) Training exclusion: Can Redwood commit that any prompt text or model outputs we send to the hosted API will NOT be used to train or improve models in any way unless we opt in? We need affirmative language that covers internal research use as well.

2) Prompt/response IP: We need the DPA (or an addendum) to state that customer-provided prompts and generated responses are treated as Customer Data and that Greenleaf retains any ownership/rights to those outputs.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border: Please confirm current subprocessors and whether you transfer EU customer data to the US. If so, we need to understand safeguards (SCCs, encryption at rest, key control).

4) Opt-out mechanics: If we opt out of model improvement, how is that enforced? Will you provide an API flag or per-account setting and can this be audited?

We attached our standard DPA redlines to the email for reference. We are trying to get procurement sign-off this week; a short summary addressing the four points above is ideal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Elena
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Greenleaf Health

Attachment: Greenleaf_DPA_Redlines.docx (document stub)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Elena Hernandez <elena.hernandez@greenleaf.health>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:55:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — training exclusion, prompt ownership, cross-border transfers

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'll follow up with our legal/ops team and provide proposed DPA language by EOD tomorrow.

1) Training exclusion
- Yes: Redwood offers a formal "no-model-improvement" option for customer data. We can include contract language that customer data will not be used to improve models (no-weights-update, no embedding pooling, no prompt/response retention beyond session retention) unless the customer explicitly opts in.
- Implementation: opt-out is implemented as an account-level flag that prevents data from being written to any internal improvement pipelines and disables sampling for research.

2) Prompt/response ownership
- We treat prompts and responses as Customer Data for customers who select the contractual option. We can add explicit ownership and licensing text in the DPA/addendum: customer retains rights to prompts & outputs; Redwood receives a limited license to process for the purposes of fulfilling the service (delivery, routing, and debugging with consent).

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers
- Current core subprocessors: AWS (eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west3) for backups, Sentry for error monitoring, and Datadog. We'll provide an up-to-date subprocessor list link and an exportable CSV.
- Cross-border: Hosted requests from EU customers may be routed to US GPUs for capacity reasons in our hosted tier. We support EU-only residency on Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts, we rely on SCCs and encrypted transfers; customer-managed keys are available on Dedicated & Private.

4) Opt-out mechanics & auditability
- Mechanic: account flag + token metadata to mark data as "no-improve". Enforcement: a combination of policy gating and runtime checks.
- Auditability: we can provide an audit log export showing that the no-improve flag was set for requests and a one-time attestation from the engineering team. For ongoing audits we can discuss a SOC-type control narrative or a scoped attestation.

Next steps: I'll push proposed DPA clauses to the Drive and loop in our contracts lawyer for final redlines. If Greenleaf needs wording faster, we can prepare an addendum that covers the three items above.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (contract stub)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — technical enforcement notes

Lauren / team — adding some technical context you can share with Elena for the procurement/infosec team: 

- Enforcement: the no-improve flag is stored in our account metadata; requests tagged as no-improve are filtered at the routing layer and are written to a separate short-lived cache only. We do not persist cache entries to any training stores.
- Logging: we retain per-request metadata for 30 days for debugging; the payload itself is not retained anywhere outside ephemeral caches when no-improve is set.
- Encryption & keys: for hosted we use provider-managed KMS; for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed KMS (CMK) so keys never leave customer control.
- SCCs: Legal can confirm, but our standard approach is to add SCCs and include a cross-border description in Schedule B of the DPA.

If Greenleaf needs a technical appendix, I can author an "Enforcement & Audit Companion" doc with sample logs and pseudocode for how the no-improve flag is enforced.

– Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren and Alex — that helps. A few follow-ups for our counsel and security team: 

- Can you provide the exact contract wording you propose for (a) the training exclusion and (b) the prompt/output ownership clause? Procurement prefers to see language we can insert in our legal review.
- For auditability: will you include an exportable audit log showing request ids and no-improve markers? Is that available for hosted accounts?
- Subprocessors: please share the CSV link for subprocessors and the date the list was last refreshed.

If you can drop the three items above into a Drive folder and share the DocuSign-ready DPA, we can route to our sign-off committee. We may request EU residency as a condition of the hosted production workload; if that's not feasible we need a written mitigation plan.

Best,
Elena

Elena — attached are the items you requested in Drive and a DocuSign envelope for the DPA + addendum that includes the training exclusion and prompt/output ownership language. Quick summary of what we attached:

- Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (clean) and Data_Processing_Addendum_markups.docx (track changes with proposed wording)
- Enforcement & Audit Companion (PDF): sample audit CSV + pseudocode for no-improve enforcement
- Subprocessor list (CSV) — refreshed 2026-07-16
- DocuSign: Docusign envelope link in Related Links; the Addendum includes: 
  * Clause 4.2.b (No-Model-Improvement): "Customer Data submitted under this Agreement shall not be used to train, tune, or improve Redwood's models, pipelines, or underlying weights unless Customer provides an explicit, documented opt-in."
  * Clause 7.1 (Customer Data Ownership): "Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in and to Customer Data, including prompts and generated outputs. Redwood is granted a limited, revocable license solely to provide the Service and for debugging with Customer consent."

On residency: for production EU residency in hosted mode we recommend Dedicated capacity (we can map the same SLA). If Greenleaf needs hosted-only EU residency, we can discuss a capacity reservation and routing guarantees but that requires a committed usage profile.

Please let us know if procurement/legal wants edits; we can turn around a redline within 24 hours. Once the DocuSign is executed we'll tag the account with the no-improve flag and provide the initial audit export.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call to finalize if helpful.

—Lauren
